rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 3 (kd 0.4, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.2, kp 1.5, sensors at x = ±0.05 and y = 0.05, score 342.03) is the best raced design. Its oval finished 16 of 20 with max_error 0.043, so derivative damping fixed the oval. Its s-bend and slalom still left the line at progress 0.28 and 0.19, with line_loss_events 0.55 and 1.0 and max_error about 0.062 to 0.064. Iteration 4 widened the outer sensors to ±0.07 and scored lower, at 271.70. The oval finish rate fell to 0.6, and s-bend and slalom progress fell to 0.17 and 0.11. Wider spacing therefore hurt, so I am reverting the x spread. Controller gains (kp 1.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.2) have not shown a clear lever on the tight tracks, and kp, ki and speed barely moved max_error across iterations 0 to 2.

Change. Starting from the iteration 3 geometry (x = ±0.05, ±0.025, 0), I move every sensor forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07. The aim is earlier steering lead on bend entry, which is where the tape is lost on the s-bend and slalom. The controller is unchanged from iteration 3, so the effect of the forward shift is isolated.

Expected result. Fewer line-loss events on s-bend and slalom (below 0.4 on s-bend, and slalom below 1.0), progress above 0.3 on those tracks, and oval finish rate held at or above 0.8. The risk is that a forward shift makes the sensors react earlier to noise, which could raise oval steering_oscillation above about 0.3.

Hypotheses. (a) Lead distance, not sensor spread, limits the tight bends. (b) If line_loss stays at 1 per run on the slalom with y = 0.07, the loss is at the sharpest bend entry, and the next test is sensor_size 0.016 at the same positions. (c) If the oval finish rate drops below 0.8 or oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.3, drop kd back toward 0.3 before changing geometry further.

Measurements wanted. Per-track progress, finish rate, line_loss_events, max_error, steering_oscillation, and distance before the first off-track event.
